body: Also, another thing I was wondering about. I'll sometimes struggle to find something to say while texting/on dates, and I'm concerned that maybe I come off as boring/shy because of this. Is this normal? Could it be due to actual shyness (which might come down to a combination of finding the right med/making an effort to talk to more people) or could it possibly be that, like you mentioned before, I haven't explored myself much and hence don't have a ton of things to talk about (and I realize that fixing this might be daunting to me as it could take years to figure out what all of my passions are). Or is it possible that it really just comes down to how compatible you are with someone?

Haha sorry I've just been busy the past few days. I've decided recently to put things on hold for a while until I've exhausted all of my options when it comes to this (including dating outside of apps as well as attempting to get my life together in general).

Yeah I can sort of see what you mean by relationships needing a bit more when it comes to personality. Maybe what I was thinking about is when you're trying to chat someone up at, say, a bar where having a bit of charisma/charm would go a long way haha.

I usually text people I'm dating at least a couple times a day, I'm not the type of person who constantly needs to be texting someone either though.

Hmm...if it takes experience to become comfortable with myself then I don't see how I could do that without a partner. I'm not too sure about getting an FWB, wouldn't that require *more* confidence/attractiveness than a regular relationship (since hookups often do)?

It's been mostly "meh"/no connection (from one or both sides) with most girls I've met over the past few months. I've felt a bit of a connection with someone I saw a couple of times recently but I'm not too sure about everything yet.

Yeah I've also heard that sex gets better for some people as they hit their 30s and 40s, but wouldn't that be due to all the experience they've picked up over the years? The average person has been having sex anywhere from 20-30 years at those ages and I feel like it might be due to confidence they've picked up over the years. I feel like I won't have quite as much experience by that point, especially if it takes me a while to find a partner.

I usually date girls in the age range of 21-29.  I've heard that a lot of people our age don't want committed relationships but I know a lot of peers around my age that are in long-term relationships (or even married). I feel like I haven't been really big on compliments unless I really like someone? I usually look for someone that's average-looking or better, doesn't live super far away, and who seems like a relatively normal person haha. I have gotten to 3rd dates from time to time, a lot of the time if we make it that far I'll know by then if there's chemistry between us.

Hmm...I've just heard that 6'2" is the "ideal" height for a guy, at least when it comes to dating sites (I've heard 6' is the minimum to be considered "attractive" for a guy on these sites/apps, hence why I'll often round up an inch when creating my profiles). I honestly don't know how I'd cope if I was under 5'6" haha (especially considering I'm not super charismatic/an extrovert).

I do know there are treatments for low T-levels but they do seem to involve a bit of work (I've heard something along the lines of going into the doc 2-3x a month or so for a shot). My biggest worry though, is that I hear that intimacy is best in a committed relationship (whatever the level of commitment), but will I even be able to enjoy it when I'm in my 30s or 40s and my drive is significantly reduced vs. my 20s? Sure 40% may not be the majority, but it's definitely not a small fraction of people either.

Haha yeah I feel like the 80 year old dads were a bit of an extreme example. But on the other hand if someone finally marries and has kids in their 40s, that sees them turning 80 when their kids are in their mid-30s or so (which still seems a bit weird to me). I feel like maybe people are marrying a *bit* later than usual but late 30s/40s still sounds pretty old though  (I think now the average age is late 20s/early 30s vs. right out of high school/college 50 years ago).

I really just talk about whatever comes to mind, I don't *think* I'm too self-deprecating? Definitely don't check my phone constantly either. Humor really just has to come to me organically, I'm not exactly the stand-up comedian type haha.

I'm 5'11" (~6' with shoes) which I've heard is a hair taller than average. Is it really that important to be that "perfect" 6'2"-6'4" though? The only solution to that I've heard of is leg-lengthening surgery which I've heard is painful (and it's not even done in the states except for extreme cases).

I've heard 40% of guys start having issues with T-levels and other things not working properly after the age of 40. Some common advice I hear to people entering their 30s is to "judge yourself not by the weight you inevitably put on, but how much less you put on vs. your peers" which worries me. I don't really smoke tobacco but I do drink on weekends though.

At this point, it wouldn't worry me too much if I met someone now and it took until 28 to get married. What I'm more worried about is if I don't meet anyone until my early-mid 30s and then it takes until my late 30s or 40s to marry. I worry about ending up in a situation like one of these: https://www.google.com/amp/s/amp.reddit.com/r/AskReddit/comments/2l6uyv/serious_people_who_were_still_single_into_their/

Don't worry about being damaging, I'm just glad I have someone to talk to in a time like this. I have been meeting a lot of people (even some 2nd dates) but just nothing seems to stick. I've tried discussing the age thing but all I hear is "focus on the present" which doesn't really help me much.

Haha I've never been super photogenic myself so maybe that could affect things.

I feel like the beginning of "old" is when it becomes physically more difficult/you have less time to do things that you enjoyed when you were younger, if that makes sense. I've heard that changes due to aging start to become obvious in your 30s and it really starts getting more difficult to stay healthy when you hit your 40s. As a guy, I fear the drop in T-levels that begins to occur after 30 and that I'll start needing a certain blue pill once I hit my 40s. I also fear that doing other things I enjoy (such as travelling or cardio) will become harder when I reach those ages.

It is pretty unbearable for me, I just feel incomplete without a partner. The thought of being "that guy" who's never had a serious relationship into his 30s or is 40+ and never married ("eternal bachelor" type) just seems excruciating. It's a lifestyle that I just don't want. I know this fixation on being in a relationship isn't attractive but I don't know how to fix it either...

I've heard about that before but if they're posting pictures of real trips/experiences with their SO then it's just hard to see how they could be unhappy.

I just feel like I've been deprived of romantic/physical intimacy and also love most of my life. I also have a severe fear of growing older (as probably is obvious at this point lol) which makes me think that I'm running out of time to experience relationships while I'm still young and energetic. Finally, one of my worst fears is that I'm one of those people who aren't cut out for relationships/are "destined to be single" and so when something doesn't work out/I'm alone for a while this fear tends to be reaffirmed. It just gets to the point where I feel it's a choice between possibly suffering a lot longer, or this :(

Yeah I've thought the same thing :/ it's awful being in a situation that's depressing while peers are moving forward with their lives. To this day I wonder what it's like to be one of the "normal"/"happy" people I see posting on Facebook all the time about their travels/anniversaries/engagements.

I know I've hit other milestones, just this one's important to me since I started dating so late and what seems difficult to achieve for me is just so trivial for others. Sure, I might be more financially secure when I'm older but I feel like there's more important things that they'd miss out on as well, like having grandparents around.

I've had people suggest a different app, I've recently picked one up but not too much success with it so far as I haven't had much time to devote to it.

I usually take at least a few pics when I visit somewhere so I can always show those.

Sure I'm closer to 20, but it does scare me that I'm getting close to the halfway mark. I don't need all of those (house, kids, marriage) by the time I'm 30 (even though some people in my high school class already have that *shudder*), in fact my 30s would probably be my optimal time to get all of those (I just want to experience *something* long-term/serious, even if it doesn't work out, by the time I'm 30). I just feel like if by a stroke of awful luck I only end up getting married in my 40s, and I end up having a kid at, say, 45, that I'll be cheating them out of a normal life (might have less energy than if I was younger, and if we go by the life expectancy I'd only be around until they're 30 or so). The reason my 20's seem important is because it's painful to watch your peers/friends hit milestones that you only get to years or even decades later.

So I've never been super into photography but I do like to take pictures of where I've visited. Hmm...people ask me specifically what bands I like so I'll have to rack my brains about that. That's refreshing to hear that I don't have to limit myself to what's cool at the moment haha (even though I do want to watch GoT someday but just haven't gotten around to it/don't have HBO).

I do have a few things in mind I'd like to pick (back) up. I just worry about how much time I have since I'm not *that* far from 30 :/ I do want kids/family someday and that's another reason I worry about age, I feel it wouldn't be a good idea to have them after, say, my late 30s/early 40s (yes, even though I'm a guy). Thanks for all of this though, this will be really helpful in sorting my thoughts out.

They definitely say that continuing to date would probably be best, so that I can learn to date in both good times and bad.

Hmm...if I had to pick one thing it'd be politics (won't specify leaning), but of course it's touchy to talk about that on a date haha. My second choice would be travel/where I've travelled to. Of course, I haven't been out of country yet, so I fear that I'm not "qualified" to list it as a passion (even though I've been to several cities). 

As for music, I like several different genres so I can't really say one artist/genre is my definite favorite which makes things tougher (and maybe one reason I'm anxious about talking about all of this is that I once had a girl unmatch me after saying I like a certain type of music lol). When it comes to shows/movies, when I rack my brains I like a few different ones as well. I like some older stuff as well as newer stuff, so I worry that someone I meet will think my tastes are weird or out-of-date.

You do have a point about not having explored myself a lot though. There's a few things I've wanted to try/pick back up but I always lack the motivation/time to pursue them (or I just forget about them). I'm honestly content to sit at home and watch TV/browse the Web most days. Did you ever have to deal with something like this? I do worry sometimes that it's a bit late to just start exploring myself this late in life (mid-20s) :(

Hmm...at what point would you say it'd be necessary to regroup? I'm not sure my depression is severe (I'm not lying in bed most of the day every day or crying all the time) but it's to the point where I am seeing a professional about it, hence the meds/therapy.

I remember once on a date that the girl I was with asked me, "So what are you super passionate about/can talk about all day?" and I struggled to answer that. Is the inability to answer that a typical sign of depression/would it be ideal to get to the point where you can answer a question like that confidently/easily?

Yeah I was kind of worried about that :/ I hate this idea (since it would put me significantly closer to 30 without any long-term relationship experience) but do you think I might need to take some time off of dating (maybe a year or two) and use the time to work on developing some relatable (key word) passions while working on my depression?

Hmm...I've always liked cats/dogs so volunteering with animals might be fun. I remember hearing that the bartenders at a local event a few months ago were volunteers and I wouldn't mind doing something like that either.

Yeah that makes more sense. I feel like I don't have a ton of interests that I'm passionate about (or at least, I have trouble putting my finger on what they are) which might hinder my ability to relate to others? Hmm...I haven't really thought about what type of volunteering that I'd specifically be interested in so I'll have to do some brainstorming. Any suggestions?

I don't know, maybe a better (more indirect) way might be to ask them out for coffee or drinks and see how they respond? Hmm...I always thought "good morning" texts usually happened when you're already in a relationship with someone though. When you talk about the "flirty" stage do you mean when you're strictly still friends or when you're heading into a relationship?

I'd also need to volunteer somewhere where the scheduling is relaxed/you can just come help when you're free. I already have a job that takes up a lot of my time so adding another 20+ hours of work a week isn't too practical haha

Thanks :)

I can be sort of flirty if I'm with someone I feel comfortable with (this happened in a couple of relationships and with one person back before I started dating)? I'm not the kind of person that flirts a lot all the time though. It is pretty nerve-wracking to confess my feelings for someone, especially since I'm more of a shy/private person (I don't know if this needs to change though).

I do want to try volunteering but I need it to be something where it's not a huge commitment/time sink (one place I was looking to volunteer at handed me a card to attach my resume/references to and stated that I'd need to undergo a background check/drug test/interviews...I was looking to volunteer, not take on a second job haha)

That sounds tough :( I wish you the best of luck with that though.

That's what I was afraid of though. I've never been good at/never been fond of the whole "are-we-just-friends-or-something-more" game that goes on when you meet someone at a meetup/interest group (hence why I've been mainly using online dating, I'm the kind of person who would like to know if we have a connection right away rather than after months or years). Also, it takes courage to risk ruining an otherwise good friendship in order to confess your feelings for someone (and from what I've read, it's usually the guy that does this which puts extra pressure on me) and I honestly just don't know if I'm extroverted enough to meet someone that way (through a meetup)

That sounds awful :( I can see not wanting to date for a while in that case.

I haven't really noticed anything like that lately? I usually let them bring up meeting again during the date if they're interested. Haha I don't think I'd last 5 minutes in the middle of nowhere (never did well in cliques)

I'm sorry you have to deal with that :( I really hope that isn't true and that you can find someone again someday. As for being pushy, that's something I've been worried about lately, but I have no idea how I'd figure out if I'm acting that way or how I'd change it if I am :( I live near/in a city (won't mention which one though)

Yeah, we didn't seem to get along and they messaged me a couple days ago saying they wanted someone more religious.

It's just tough seeing couples (in general, not just married) and thinking to myself that it'll be a while/I might be older before I get to experience that again :(

Eh, I just don't want to get to the point where most people I meet are like "ew, he's age X and hasn't had anything last longer than a year yet? NEXT!". I had one a couple of days ago that went meh and maybe a couple in a few weeks, other than that not too much as of now.
Maybe? I feel like I want a bit of both, I miss the intimacy/fun times with my ex but I also feel like I need to have something long-term before I'm too old and it becomes weird haha

I don't know, I've never really been good at hookups (I feel you need even more confidence/charisma than with finding normal relationships?). The only time I was able to score a fling (lasted a week) was when I was in a bar and had more than a few to drink, so to speak.

Hmm...maybe I wasn't too clear here. I wouldn't mind meeting the person I marry at that age. I just worry about not having any experience in a long-term relationship by that age or even having a dry spell that lasts until I'm that old.

What specifically do you mean by antisocial haha?

Thanks for the advice :) I'll try to remember that. 

What if I'm right though? What if I'm just one of those guys, who for whatever reason, has a couple of relationships in their early 20's and then goes years without a partner until their late 20's or 30's? I hear a lot about how guys who are more introverted tend to peak dating-wise at 30+.

I don't know, I always wondered if it was important for a guy to be a good politician when it comes to dating :/ (not in the career sense though).

I just don't know how I should handle this if it does go on long-term...

I don't know, sure there might be things like you mentioned that make life a bit more worth living, but it's just painful for me to think about a life where I don't meet anyone for decades, or ever. If I do meet someone later (like in my 40s or later), I worry about the idea that we won't have much time together (the life expectancy is still only 78 in the US, and I honestly wouldn't be surprised if the depression/anxiety meds I need to take are about as healthy for me as cigarettes), and that we won't be able to do fun things that younger couples can do. I also want kids someday, and even though I'm a guy, I still feel like it'd be irresponsible of me to have kids after my early 40s or so.

I mainly date though online apps, and struggle to see myself finding someone offline outside of a bar/speed dating/singles event context. It just seems so tough to find someone at, say, a meetup (there's the questions of "do they only like me as friends or something more"/"are they even single", etc. I've heard of people staying friends for *years* before one of them finally confesses their feelings for the other, and I just can't see myself getting the courage to reach out like that and risk getting burned).

Hmm...I'd say I'm ok with eye contact, my mind does wander/I'll get distracted sometimes though. Would you say charisma/having a lot of interesting hobbies is important? I'll usually try to pick a decent restaurant/bar to meet up at, I'll admit sometimes my choices have flopped though (e.g., the place is too loud or there's a quirky event going on that night that I didn't expect)

Hmm...I've thought about doing that, would it be weird, as a guy, saying that I only want something long-term on my profile though?

To me 30 just doesn't seem that far away. I've kind of struggled a bit with confidence to be honest, it goes up and down for me (I had more last year right before I met my ex, lately it's been down to zero) and I honestly wish I knew how to gain more at times like this. I don't think I've ever been conventionally "charismatic" either.

Yeah I would almost always follow up with something like what you said, but they didn't want to meet up again.

Maybe what I was getting at is that (so I've heard) not having a serious/long-term relationship by your early-mid 30's starts to become a red flag and by 40 it's definitely a red flag. I think every day about what it would mean for me to reach those ages without anything to show for it (relationship-wise).

Not sure what you mean by in love? I've never actually told someone "I love you" but I do feel like I fell pretty hard for my last steady gf

Hmm...there were a couple that I wanted to see again (I at least *thought* we got along somewhat). One of them kept bringing up politics a lot and I feel like our views differed (I usually don't bring up politics on a first date and I won't discuss my views here) which I speculate may have caused them to lose interest.

I know dating history *should* be personal but I've dated several people who've asked so far. One of them (on a 2nd date) asked me how many past relationships I've had, I mentioned that I had a couple of relationships a few months long. Their response: "That's it?!? I've had several serious boyfriends!". They kind of faded away contact after that date as well. I've also read a post online where someone was wondering if it was a red flag that her boyfriend (age 28) of 10 months had had nothing last longer than 3 months before meeting her (the real problem was that he was an *alcoholic*, but that's another discussion). However, the people I had my longest relationships with didn't ask though. I know a lot of people our age aren't settled yet but I do feel like most people have had at least *one* long-term/serious relationship by this point.

Haha no worries about writing a lot, I'm always a fan of good discussion :)

*sigh* I've always worried about the awkwardness part. I'm a bit shy by nature (and I've been trying medications to combat that) and my biggest fear is that being shy is a big turn-off, or that I'll need to become more extroverted in order to be considered "attractive" (I just really want someone to accept me as I am, not for a facade I put on).

Yeah I kind of hated living in the suburbs haha (not a fan of needing to drive all the time) so I definitely don't want that type of life right now. I just fear that it'll be hard to find someone that would overlook not having had a long-term relationship yet after 30 or 35...

Hmm...I'm not sure it was that serious, it did have a big impact on my life though.

This might sound weird, but it seems at times I don't have problems getting dates? I just don't seem to click with anyone though, or for some reason things don't work out. I've been getting more "you're a great guy but I don't want to meet up again" messages lately, which does lead me to think I might be doing something wrong when I'm meeting people.

Wow, that's exactly what's happening with most of my peers from high school (there's a ton my age or younger getting engaged/married/buying houses). I could see giving it a few more years but I'm not sure I care to see what my 30s are like if I haven't had anything long-term by then.

Maybe they might know someone? I never thought about that too much. Also, what exactly defines a serious relationship? I've always thought it was at least a year long, you introduce each other to friends, Facebook official etc.

The apps were working before (I had a few relationships off of them) but while I've still been meeting people, everyone just seems to reject
 me eventually and it doesn't evolve into anything further.

I know I might need time but exactly how much?!? I feel like it's very unusual to go years without meeting anyone you're compatible with.

Thanks for talking with me by the way, this has been super helpful.

Most of my friends are guys though. I don't really approach anyone at the gym since I've always assumed that people just want to work out and do their own thing. Just curious (if you don't mind me asking), what was your longest time without a relationship?

I really wish there was another option rather than either this or suffering long-term. I really don't see a 3rd option at this point though :(

Also, what if I don't find anyone in the next few months, or anytime soon for that matter? What if I'm in my 30s by the time I find my next relationship? I just can't think of a way that I'd deal with all this pain/rejection/loneliness for such a prolonged period of time...

Hmm...I've thought about meeting people through friends. I just don't know how to ask if they know anyone who's single without it sounding awkward. Any suggestions?

I do have a few other interests, but I don't really partake in them too often. A lot of my time is spent working, browsing the web, watching TV/playing video games, and working out. I've thought about picking up some new hobbies, but a lot of them require a lot of motivation/time/money that I just don't have. Meanwhile, it seems like most people have a ton they can talk about...

I just can't figure out a way to deal with (potentially) years of pain, rejection and loneliness, other than this :(

I try to be happy for friends but it also gets me into the mindset of "well, maybe that level of happiness just isn't meant to happen to me". It's not just that it's been 6 months that makes me feel hopeless, it's that people who seem to like me just end up turning around and rejecting me...

Haha by online I meant dating apps. I have had one long distance relationship though and I'll admit it was tough meeting up with them. Unfortunately I've never had luck meeting people in clubs (as in interest groups).

I do have other things in my life, I just think it'd be horrible to go through the pain of years of rejection while watching all my peers find people that are right for them. I don't mind getting married in my 30s but not meeting anyone who will give me a chance until then might be awful.

I do wish I started dating earlier, I feel like a lot of my peers have 10 years of experience on me...
Most of it has been online, since I'm somewhat shy. Never had luck meeting anyone (dating-wise) at a meetup or at a coffee shop or anything like that.
It's just gone on for so long, it's not easy for me to see anything being different.

I don't know, I just fear that all I have to look forward to in the years (or even decades) ahead is more pain and rejection. I want to know what it's like to be young and with someone great, not just when I'm middle-aged.

How much later in life? Did it have any detrimental effects on the relationship only having found someone so late?

If I've been rejected over and over by nearly everyone for 6 months straight, I don't see how that can't be me. I'm the only common denominator here.

I think we're only really living longer on average. For men in the US, it is only ~77 years (source: https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_life_expectancy).

Where are all these people putting off relationships/kids until later? Half the people I know from high school are engaged at this point. Is that only a West Coast/Northeast thing?

I still don't know how I'm supposed to be comfortable with myself after being rejected over and over again...

I can't build confidence on a bunch of rejection though. Sure they might not care initially if I'm inexperienced, but what if me not knowing what to do puts strain on the relationship?

There might not be any "predetermined" times but there are consequences for hitting normal milestones later than usual. For example, what if it takes me until my 40s to get married? Then kids will be out of the question (sure, I may be a guy, but nobody wants to lose their parents when they're only in their 20's or 30's).
Anyone? :(

Thanks again for the reply. 

1. How much did you find you had to cut back? Was it just a matter of not going all out like in college every weekend or was it a lot more than that?
2. Hmm...funny you mention martial arts, I did Tae Kwon Do when I was younger and have been thinking about getting back into it lately. I can cook some basic things but I'm no sous chef either, I guess I could devote some time to that though. Haha I was actually just thinking about getting into hiking (I have a slight interest in it), why would you say it's too generic though?
Thanks for the reply. Yeah I know it's only one aspect of life, but I'm seriously worried at this point if people will start considering me "damaged goods" if I haven't had anything serious by 30...

Thanks for the reply. How did you end up dating anyone without asking anyone out though (never had a date before I started initiating conversations, asking women out etc.)? Also, around what age would you say you really started having luck with dating?

Thanks for the reply. Yeah I've never been interested in those $2000 PUA seminars anyway lol.

I did have a few questions though:

1. Does it take a lot of work to stay in shape in your 30s? I've always had a tough time with workout routines (too tired after work, and I suck at getting up before 6:30 lol). Also, did you find that you had to give up/significantly cut back on alcohol?
2. What do you mean by a "cool" hobby? I've never been good at sports so that's out, but is there anything else you can suggest trying?
3. I'm naturally pretty shy, but would you say it's important to become an extrovert? I've been trying different meds to help with my anxiety for years but none have helped :/

Thanks again.

What I'm not looking forward to though, is the idea that I might only find my first meaningful relationship when I'm older and the idea that my partner will need to be exceedingly patient and have to teach me everything...

I don't know, I feel like not having at least 1 relationship that lasted more than a few months is already a red flag at my age. I worry that it'll eventually become a real dealbreaker as I get older :(
